subject: Reschedule: Redwood demo — calendar resource created a hostless Meet, propose dial-in fallback
messages:
From: Sam Lee <sam@greenlineanalytics.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Greenline Procurement <procurement@greenlineanalytics.com>
Date: 2028-01-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Demo this week — join link broken for several guests

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for sending over the invite for the Redwood demo tomorrow. A few of our attendees (including procurement) tried to join and are seeing the Meet entry show "No host" and the Meet join button is either absent or routes to a generic calendar event without a link. I attached a screenshot.

We're running SSO and some of our users are on a managed GSuite domain — we've seen calendar resource-created invites strip host tokens before. Procurement is sensitive about stable audit trails in invites, so this is blocking them from accepting.

Can you:
- Confirm whether the invite was created under a resource calendar or under an individual organizer?
- If it's a resource issue, can you regenerate the invite under a Redwood user account?
- As a short-term fallback, could you provide a phone dial-in (conference number) so we can all join tomorrow?

Sam
Sam Lee
Senior Data Platform Lead
Greenline Analytics
[attachment: calendar-screenshot.png (image/png)]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam@greenlineanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-10T09:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Demo this week — join link broken for several guests

On Tue, Jan 10, 2028 at 09:12 AM Sam Lee <sam@greenlineanalytics.com> wrote:
> Hi Evelyn,
>
> Thanks for sending over the invite for the Redwood demo tomorrow. A few of our attendees (including procurement) tried to join and are seeing the Meet entry show "No host"...

Thanks for the heads up, Sam — sorry for the friction. I double-checked the event: it looks like the calendar entry was created by our team automation and it created the event on a shared resource calendar (demo-room@redwood.com) rather than an individual host account. Some resource calendars do not preserve the meet host metadata when forwarded/accepted across domains.

I'm looping in Ben (SE) and Monica (CS ops) to help: Ben can provision a temporary Zoom bridge and phone numbers; Monica can re-issue the calendar invite under a user account so the host token stays intact.

Short-term plan:
- Ben to publish a dial-in + Zoom bridge today as a fallback (we'll include PST and toll numbers)
- Monica to regenerate the calendar invite from ben.carter@redwood.com (explicit host) and include procurement in the To: field so their acceptance is tracked
- If those don't work, we can reschedule to Fri 1/12 10:00 AM PST when we can guarantee a Zoom host present.

I've attached the draft demo agenda so procurement can review while we sort the invite.

Evelyn Hart
Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
[attachment: demo-agenda.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Sam Lee <sam@greenlineanalytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-10T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Demo this week — provisioning Zoom bridge + dial-in fallback

Hi all,

I can stand up a temporary Zoom meeting and PST dial-in numbers for tomorrow. A few notes so we avoid the hostless behavior:
- Create the meeting under the individual host account that will actually click "Start meeting" (e.g., ben.carter@redwood.com). Resource calendars sometimes strip the encrypted host token when events are forwarded or when external domains accept — that results in the "No host" UX.
- I'll regenerate the invite from my account and include Sam + procurement in the To list. That will preserve host ownership.
- I'll publish both the Meet link (if needed) and the Zoom bridge + dial-in in the event body; attendees can choose.

If procurement requires a formal audit trail (invite acceptance logs), Monica: could you attach the audit checklist to the regenerated invite? Sam: do you need a specific dial-in country code besides US/PST?

I'll send the regenerated invite in ~20 minutes and include the Zoom details and phone numbers.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-connection-guide.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

From: Sam Lee <sam@greenlineanalytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Greenline Procurement <procurement@greenlineanalytics.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-11T15:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Demo this week — provisioning Zoom bridge + dial-in fallback

Thanks Ben — that worked. We received the regenerated invite from ben.carter@redwood.com and the Zoom + dial-in details are in the event body. Procurement confirmed they could accept the invite and the join button is visible for our SSO users.

Confirming we'll keep the slot: Fri, Jan 12, 2028 at 10:00 AM PST. Monica — procurement asked if you can attach the compliance checklist to the calendar event and drop the final agenda in the invite thread.

Sam
Sam Lee
Senior Data Platform Lead
Greenline Analytics
